---
title: ODI lineup experiment
---

## Question and data exposure

Does including player identities improve future-match win probabilities beyond a
team-only model for decisive, fixed-XI ODIs in the available Cricsheet sample?
The primary contrast is combined team-plus-player versus team-only mean log loss,
separately for men's and women's matches. Player-only prediction is secondary.
This is a predictive comparison, not a causal estimate of selecting a player.

This specification was written before fitting these models. Match counts and the
preparation code's outcomes were already accessible; this is a self-attested
development protocol, not a registered or blinded study.

## Sample and information

Use `lineup_eligible=1` matches and require eleven distinct identified participants
per side. Retain all such decisive results, including shortened matches. Ties,
no-results, and matches involving replacements remain outside this initial binary
experiment. Replacement status is known retrospectively: evaluation is conditional
on this restricted sample, not an operational forecast of every scheduled ODI.

Team A is the alphabetically first team. Its win indicator is the response.
Use only team identities, selected players, and toss winner/decision as predictors.
The toss winner contributes +1 for A, -1 for B; the team choosing or being sent
in to bat contributes +1 for A, -1 for B. Missing toss information contributes zero
for the corresponding feature. Venue/home effects await an audited venue mapping;
this team benchmark is not a claim to match the best available team forecast.

## Models

Fit three ridge logistic models: team effects; player effects; and both. All
include the same two toss terms. Encode each entity as +1 for A and -1 for B,
and fit without an intercept. Swapping the sides must complement the prediction.

Use scikit-learn `LogisticRegression` with `l1_ratio=0`, `solver="lbfgs"`,
`fit_intercept=False`, `tol=1e-8`, `max_iter=2000`, and no class weighting.
The objective is summed binary log loss plus `sum(beta**2)/(2*C)`.
All coefficients, including context, receive the same penalty within a model.
Combined-model attribution between team and player effects therefore depends on
this penalty convention; it is not separately identified institutional value.
Treat convergence warnings as failed fits rather than silently accepting them.

Fit feature vocabularies on training matches only. Unseen entities contribute
zero, the shrinkage center. Export counts of unseen players and teams per forecast.
Do not use names or career exposure from later matches to label an earlier fit.

## Chronological evaluation

Evaluate calendar years 2023, 2024, and 2025 separately. The primary training
window is five calendar years preceding each evaluation year; a three-year window
is a pre-specified sensitivity analysis. Within each window, reserve the last
calendar year for validation. Fit on earlier years, select `C` from
`[0.01, 0.1, 1, 10]` by validation log loss, then refit using the whole window.
Break exact ties toward smaller `C`. Retain every tuning score and every
evaluation prediction. If a split lacks observations or training has only one
outcome class, fail explicitly. Do not silently alter the split or pool genders.

The fitted model stays fixed throughout the evaluation year. Later annual fits
may use earlier evaluation years as historical training data, as in a rolling
forecast exercise. The preparation cutoff must cover each whole evaluation year.
Source revisions mean this backtest is not proof of data availability at each
historical cutoff.

Use start dates to assign validation and evaluation cohorts. Training and refitting
require completion before the relevant cutoff. A match that starts before a cutoff
and finishes after it is neither available for training at that cutoff nor a new
forecast at that cutoff. Refit on all completed matches in the window, including
any such boundary match once its result is available. Quarter blocks use match
start dates. These rules were clarified during independent design review
before estimation.

## Metrics and uncertainty

Report annual and pooled match-weighted log loss, Brier score, and five fixed
calibration bins spanning [0, 1]. Include a 0.5 probability reference. Export
paired loss differences between each lineup model and the team baseline.
Differences are lineup minus team; negative differences favor the lineup model.

For pooled differences, resample whole calendar quarters with replacement, using
2,000 replicates and seed 20261027. Each replicate retains every match within
each sampled quarter, and divides summed loss differences by the number of
sampled matches. Report percentile 95% intervals and the number of nonempty blocks.
This preserves some within-period dependence, including many series and tournament
matches. It does not guarantee independence across quarters, and 2023–2025 provide
at most twelve blocks. These are exploratory intervals conditional on fitted
forecasts, not full uncertainty from training, tuning, or player identification.
No multiplicity-adjusted hypothesis tests or significance declarations are planned.

## Attribution and acceptance

Export coefficients in log-odds units, training appearances, the fraction of a
player's matches shared with their most frequent teammate, and exact identical
appearance-pattern groups. Perfectly co-occurring players cannot be distinguished
by these outcomes. Also record connected components of the training opponent
network. Ridge coefficients are finite even when individual attribution is weak.
Do not export ranks, player confidence intervals, WAR, or current-strength claims
from this static experiment.

Test swap symmetry, unseen-player handling, cutoff leakage, coefficient recovery
on simulated changing lineups, and exact co-occurrence before fitting real data.
Validate input hashes and output provenance. Obtain an independent design/code
review before the first real-data fit.

If added player identities do not improve the team benchmark, retain that finding.
If improvement changes across windows or genders, report the variation. Better
prediction would justify further modeling, not validate individual rankings.
Dynamic strength, wicket valuation, replacement calibration, and WPA remain
separate next stages.

## Deviations

None at specification time. Later changes and their reasons will be recorded here.

## Independent review before estimation

An independent model reviewed the design and core code before real-data fitting.
The review checked the shrinkage objective, swap symmetry, and unequal-size block
resampling on synthetic data. It requested explicit calendar-boundary handling,
refit sample IDs, and exported match-level paired losses; these are included.
The review found no additional blocker for this limited predictive comparison.
It emphasized that effective shrinkage, omitted venue/time variation, and weak
individual identification remain interpretation limits.
